newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative Party overhaul urgent - Dorrell.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative Party overhaul urgent - Dorrell.

text.p: Britain's Conservative Party must learn the lessons of its stinging election defeat and become as effective a fighting force as Labour within a year, former health secretary Stephen Dorrell said on Tuesday.

Dorrell, one of six declared candidates to succeed John Major as party leader, said he would seek the support of the National Union (the party's voluntary side) and Conservative agents for an immediate review of the party's structure.

The purpose would be to establish a new constitution for the party that welds together its different parts into a more cohesive and disciplined whole, Dorrell said in a letter to all Conservative constituency association chairmen.
"One inescapable lesson of our general election defeat is that, for the first time, our opponents were better organised and more disciplined than we were.
"The most urgent priority facing the new leader is to ensure that this deficit is reveresed and that the Conservative Party organisation is re-established as the best in the business," Dorrell said.
